title: Book Three · Chapter 54: The Longer Question
story:
The new term begins on Monday.

Ronan finds his desk beside the window. Anna is already there. Her maths book looks thicker because several loose sheets are inside it.

“More windows?” he asks.

“Some walls too.”

Kai puts his bag at the next desk. He has brought a new ruler and the same old ball.

“Only one is for the lesson,” Anna says.

“I know which one.”

Kai sits down as the teacher comes in.

The morning work starts with familiar things. Then the teacher gives them a page of longer questions.

Ronan reads the first one. He knows the words, but there are several numbers. Some belong to a wall. Others belong to the door and window inside it.

The question asks about paint. Only part of the wall needs it.

Ronan draws a rectangle in his notebook. He writes a number beside each side. Then he looks back at the question.

He has not used all the numbers. He does not know which to use next.

Beside him, Anna draws a smaller rectangle inside her first one. She pauses too, but only for a moment.

Ronan wants to ask. The teacher is explaining another example at the board, so he listens first.

He moves his pencil toward the new example. Its window has a different shape from his window.

He starts to copy the numbers, then stops. Those are the teacher's numbers. His own question is still beside his elbow.

He writes WALL above his large rectangle. The word makes the drawing easier to find, but it does not finish the sum.

At the front, the teacher points to two lines. Ronan follows the pencil with his eyes. He understands the first part and loses the next.

He looks around. One student is still on the first question. Another has turned the page.

Ronan brings his finger back to his own drawing. He puts a little mark beside the last step he understands. Then he leaves enough room below it to try the rest again.

When the teacher moves to another question, he keeps his own page open. He wants to ask for help with this drawing, not with a whole page of copied numbers.

At the end of the lesson, he has two answers and one half-finished drawing.

“Can you show me that one?” he asks Anna.

“After school?”

“Today?”

She looks at the page in her own notebook. There are two short plans near the top.

“Not today. I promised Lin a run. I have my own new work this week too. Wednesday next week, for a little while?”

Ronan wants the answer before then. He looks at the drawing again.

“Next Wednesday. I will try it tonight too.”

“Good. Bring the part that stops you.”

At lunch, Kai looks at his own page. His first drawing is neat. His written explanation is only three words.

“Mine needs paint and words,” he says.

Ronan laughs. “I have words. Not the right answer.”

They eat and go outside. For ten minutes, the ball needs no rectangles.

That evening, Ronan finishes the ninth letter to Leo. He tells him about the new questions and the hall visit planned for Saturday. Anna's window question is still at the top.

He sends it at the post office before he starts the rest of his work.

At home, Mum asks him to move his paper away from her scissors. He takes the unfinished drawing to his end of the table.

This time, he crosses out the door inside the large rectangle. No paint will go there.

He writes one more line beneath it. Then he opens the next question and reads the last sentence first.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

rectangle＝长方形；paint＝油漆、涂刷；half-finished＝做了一半的；explanation＝解释。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan这次遇到的困难是不是单个词都不认识？墙面题里为什么有些部分不用涂漆？
2. Anna答应什么时候帮他？Ronan在等待之前采取了什么行动？

## 读句子

**He writes one more line beneath it.**

拆开看：He / writes one more line / beneath it.

他／再写下一行／写在图下面。
